baseline:
C
An infinite series is the sum of a sequence with an unlimited number of terms. While some series diverge to infinity, many converge to a finite value.

B
A convergent series has a sum that approaches a specific, finite value as more terms are added. A divergent series does not; its sum either grows infinitely large (positively or negatively) or oscillates without settling on a single value.

B
The convergence of a series depends on its sequence of partial sums approaching a limit. The "closeness" or distance between two numbers on the real line (like a partial sum and its limit) is formally measured by the absolute value of their difference, `|x - y|`.

B
In the 2-adic metric, the distance between two numbers, x and y, is determined by the highest power of 2 that divides their difference (x-y). If their difference is divisible by a very high power of 2, the 2-adic distance between them is very small, meaning they are "close".

C
In the 2-adic metric, the "size" of a number is determined by its divisibility by 2. The term 2^n becomes vanishingly small as n increases. This allows the geometric series formula to be used, yielding a sum of a / (1 - r) = 1 / (1 - 2) = -1.
